segments.text: ♪ (intro music) ♪
Flutter has a ton of widgets that describe
how the components of an app's UI  should look and behave.
If you've built an app with Flutter, you're probably very familiar with them.
What you might not know is that Flutter also has a widget
that can describe  what a piece of the UI means.
That widget is Semantics.
Imagine a screen in a contacts app
that has two widgets in a stack-- a background and a circular avatar.
One of those widgets  is very significant and one is not.
That's an important thing  for screen readers, search engines
and other semantic analysis tools to know.
You can provide that information by wrapping each widget with Semantics.
Semantics has a bunch of properties
for things like text descriptions,
whether the widget should be considered enabled or disabled,
even whether it represents  an input element or a read-only field.
And that's not all.
Semantics has almost  50 properties you can use
to provide additional meaning for your UI.
For more information on those and all the other Flutter widgets,
head to flutter.dev.
♪ (outro music) ♪
